items.title: Four Supports for Correct View in Both Activity and Stillness, the Three Knowledges and Two Liberations, and What Grounds All Physical Matter

items.zh: 又有四種能得正見無倒義行所依處所。由前三種，行時清淨；由後一種，住時清淨。謂守根門者，於諸境界不順不違，為守根門念增上力，正智而行。住遠離者、心無染污、專注一緣。又由四行，當知能證明及解脫。由念、眼、慧、能證於明；又由身故，能證不動及時解脫。復有四法，能為廣大種種差別諸所造色生起依止。一者、堅性，二者、濕性，三者、煖性，四者、輕等動性。又有四法，能持已生諸有情類令得久住，及能攝益尋求有者。
items.en: There are also four bases for attaining correct, undistorted view and conduct: the first three purify one while active, the last purifies one while abiding still. Namely: guarding the sense-doors, neither favouring nor opposing any object; the power of mindfulness that sustains this guarding; and acting with clear comprehension. One who dwells in seclusion keeps the mind free of defilement, focused single-pointedly on one object. By four factors, know that the [three] knowledges and [two] liberations are realised: by mindfulness, by the [divine] eye, and by wisdom, the three knowledges are realised; and by the body, unshakeable liberation and time-liberation are realised. There are also four things that give rise to the great variety of matter that arises from them: first, solidity; second, moisture; third, heat; fourth, lightness and mobility. There are also four things that sustain already-arisen sentient beings in continued existence and draw those still seeking further existence towards it.

items.title: Four Ways Consciousness Clings to the Aggregates, and Four Kinds of Craving Even a Sincere Monk Must Watch For

items.zh: 又有四種於生死中諸識流轉所依足迹。謂於諸色見已趣向；由貪愛故，取為所緣；所依、境界俱有建立。如於諸色，於受、想、行、當知亦爾。又諸苾芻，顧戀現法身命為依止故，而於衣服、飲食、臥具生希求愛；顧戀後法身命為依止故，而於後有生悕求愛；愚於涅槃為依止故，而於無有生悕求愛。如是略有四種悕求之愛。謂衣服愛、飲食愛、臥具愛、有無有愛。
items.en: There are also four footprints on which consciousness's flux through birth and death depends. Namely: having seen form, one turns towards it; through craving, one grasps it as an object; and the support and the object are both thereby established together. As with form, know that it is likewise so with feeling, perception, and formations. Further, monks, cherishing the body and life of the present existence as their basis, give rise to craving desire for clothing, food, and bedding; cherishing the body and life of a future existence as their basis, they give rise to craving for further existence; and, deluded with respect to nirvāṇa as their basis, they give rise to craving for non-existence. Thus, briefly, there are four kinds of craving desire: craving for clothing, for food, for bedding, and for existence or non-existence.

items.title: Four Roots Driving Unwholesome Action, and the Four Correct Ways to Answer a Question

items.zh: 又有四法，能令有情現行造作所不應作。謂隨順可愛事，違逆不可愛事，怖畏強敵其心顛倒，愚於現法及後法果。又有四種請問記論，能斷所疑，能悟未悟，又能任持勝決擇力。謂於法實相應一向記，於諸有情業果異熟應分別記，於隱密說非一向問應詰問記，於不如理應當置記。於此問中，云何名記？謂記彼問，言佛世尊於斯不記。
items.en: There are also four things that cause sentient beings to act in ways they should not: yielding to what is agreeable; resisting what is disagreeable; fearing a formidable opponent, the mind thereby inverted; and being deluded regarding the fruit of both this life and the next. There are also four kinds of response to a question, capable of severing doubt, awakening the unawakened, and sustaining the power of superior discernment: with respect to the true nature of phenomena, one should answer directly; with respect to sentient beings' karmic ripening, one should answer analytically; with respect to a question that is ambiguous or not single in intent, one should answer by counter-question; and with respect to what is unreasonable, one should set the question aside.

items.title: Four Grades of Giving by Giver and Recipient's Purity, the Four Means of Gathering a Following, and Four Modes of Rebirth

items.zh: 又有四種惠捨，或清淨，或不清淨。三種清淨，謂唯自身戒見具足，或復唯他戒見具足，或自及他戒見具足；一、不清淨，謂自及他戒見二種俱不具足。其清淨者，當生善趣，資產豐饒；不清淨者，當生惡趣，資產無匱。又有四種攝眾方便，能正攝化一切大眾。一、饒益方便，二、攝受方便，三、引導方便，四、修治方便。又有四種從業所生諸有情類，於彼彼趣生依止門。一、由業及卵㲉，二、由業及胎膜，三、由業及潤污，四、唯由業。
items.en: There are also four kinds of giving, either pure or impure. Three are pure: where only one's own precepts and view are complete, where only the other's are complete, or where both one's own and the other's are complete. One is impure: where neither one's own nor the other's precepts and view are complete. The pure kinds lead to a favourable rebirth abundant in resources; the impure kind leads to an unfavorable rebirth, yet not lacking in resources. There are also four skilful means of gathering a following, capable of rightly drawing in and transforming the entire community: first, the means of benefiting; second, the means of gathering in; third, the means of guiding; fourth, the means of cultivating together. There are also four gateways by which sentient beings, born from karma, take up existence in this or that destiny: first, by karma together with an eggshell; second, by karma together with a womb-membrane; third, by karma together with moisture; fourth, by karma alone.

items.title: Four Kinds of Death by Cause, and Two Frameworks for the Graded Purity of the Path to Realisation

items.zh: 又彼彼處受生有情有四種死。一者、由自故死，謂於戲忘、意忿天中而受生者。二、由他故死。謂於羯羅藍、頞部曇、閉尸、鍵南母腹中者。三、俱由故死，謂在欲界所餘有情。四、俱不由故死，謂色無色界有頂為後所有有情。復有四清淨道。一、非功用根圓滿，亦非喜樂圓滿；二、功用根圓滿，非喜樂圓滿；三、喜樂圓滿，非功用根圓滿；四、喜樂圓滿，亦功用根圓滿。又有四清淨道。一、背惡說法及毘奈耶，二、向善說法及毘奈耶，三、資糧道，四、清淨道。
items.en: Sentient beings reborn in various places die by four causes: first, by their own cause — those reborn among the gods of frivolous play or of malicious anger; second, by another's cause — those in the mother's womb at the kalala, arbuda, peśī, and ghana stages; third, by both causes — the remaining beings of the desire realm; fourth, by neither cause — beings of the form and formless realms up through the peak of existence. There are also four purities of the path: first, neither effort of the faculties nor bliss and joy is complete; second, effort of the faculties is complete, but not bliss and joy; third, bliss and joy is complete, but not effort of the faculties; fourth, both bliss and joy and effort of the faculties are complete. There are also [another] four purities of the path: first, turning away from wrongly taught doctrine and discipline; second, turning towards rightly taught doctrine and discipline; third, the path of gathering provisions; fourth, the path of purity.

items.zh: 此中最初，謂如有一，於外道見及引無義苦切行中，心不愛樂，亦不忍可。第二、謂如有一，於蘊、界、處、緣起、處非處等諸善巧中，愛樂忍可；又能堪忍寒熱等苦。第三、謂淨尸羅、守根門等諸善資糧所攝正法。第四、謂奢摩他、毘鉢舍那斷諸煩惱現法樂住。

blocks.text: The fours continue. Today includes a practical list every teacher can use, the four ways to answer a question, and the four means of gathering a following, the bodhisattva's social method.

subs.head: Supports for right view; knowledges and liberations

blocks.text: Right view is supported in activity and in stillness. The three knowledges and two liberations (Day 65) are realised "by mindfulness, eye, and wisdom": the *Pīxún jì* matches recollection of past lives with mindfulness, knowledge of death and rebirth with the eye, and the ending of the outflows with wisdom.

Consciousness clings to four "stations": form, feeling, perception, and formations. Venerable Miào Jìng: consciousness "delights in dwelling" on them, taking them as a happy home. Liberation is consciousness no longer settling anywhere.

Among them is craving for non-existence. Venerable Miào Jìng's sobering example: a person in great pain who wishes to end his life, imagining that death is nirvāṇa. The treatise's account of rebirth (Days 5–6) shows why this is a delusion: the stream does not stop at death.

What should not be done is driven by four roots. Venerable Miào Jìng names them greed, hatred, fear, and delusion; Master Cháng Bǎi, with the *Pīxún jì*, greed, hatred, wrong view, and ignorance. Venerable Miào Jìng's addition of fear is worth noticing: much wrongdoing is done out of fear of someone more powerful.

The **four kinds of answer** (四記論): **direct** answer, **analytical** answer, answer by **counter-question**, and **setting aside** (Day 1's commentary on the opening question-and-answer). Master Cháng Bǎi: direct and analytical answers sever doubt; the counter-question brings the questioner to understand for himself; setting aside protects him from a question that cannot help.

Four grades of giving are defined by the purity of giver and recipient (the *Pīxún jì* reads "self" and "other" as the owner of the gift and the one who hands it over). The **four means of gathering** (四攝事): **generosity**, **kind speech**, **beneficial action**, and **acting alike** with others. These are how a bodhisattva draws people towards the Dharma: give first, speak kindly, help in practical ways, and share their life.

Four modes of birth (Day 13). Four kinds of death by cause, including death "by one's own cause", such as the gods of malicious anger. Master Cháng Bǎi: they "glare at each other whenever they meet" and die of rage (Day 33).

subs.head: Two frameworks for the path's purity

blocks.text: The path's purity is graded two ways. Venerable Miào Jìng, plainly, on who has "dull faculties" in the first: "the lazy one, whose roots of good are imperfectly cultivated", yet enough to attain the path.

quiz.q: The treatise names four footprints on which consciousness depends. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say "consciousness abiding" means?
options: consciousness delights to dwell on form, feeling, perception, and formations, deeming them a happy place — that is, clinging
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: consciousness delights in dwelling on form, feeling, perception, and formations, taking them as a happy place — that is, attachment. The treatise: having seen form, one turns towards it and, through craving, grasps it as object.

quiz.q: The treatise says, deluded about nirvāṇa, one craves non-existence. What example does Venerable Miào Jìng give?
options: a person in great pain who wants to commit suicide, thinking that is entering nirvāṇa and liberation
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "A person in severe pain wants to commit suicide, thinking that after suicide he has entered nirvāṇa, attained liberation." Craving for non-existence is a wrong view, worse even than craving existence.

quiz.q: How do the two teachers name the four roots driving what should not be done?
options: Miào Jìng: greed, hatred, fear, delusion; Cháng Bǎi citing the Pixunji: greed, hatred, wrong view, ignorance
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: yielding to the agreeable is greed, resisting the disagreeable is hatred, fear of a strong enemy is fear, delusion about this and the next life is delusion. The *Pixunji*, cited by Master Cháng Bǎi, gives greed, hatred, wrong view, and ignorance.

quiz.q: The four kinds of answer sever doubt, awaken the unawakened, and sustain discernment. How does Master Cháng Bǎi map them?
options: direct and analytical answers sever doubt, counter-question awakens, setting aside sustains certainty
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: among the four, direct and analytical answers sever doubt; the counter-question brings the unawakened to awaken; setting aside sustains certainty. Venerable Miào Jìng's example of a question to set aside: is a barren woman's son white or black?

quiz.q: In the four kinds of giving, the English takes 自 and 他 as giver and recipient. How do the lectures read them?
options: the owner of the wealth and the agent who hands it over in the same act of giving — not the recipient
self is the Buddha, other is beings
self is this life, other the next
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: "If one gives another's goods by one's own hand, the agent is 'self' and the owner 'other'; if one has another give one's own goods, the owner is 'self' and the agent 'other.'" Venerable Miào Jìng concurs.

quiz.q: The first death, "by one's own cause," includes the gods of malicious anger. How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe them?
options: gods with great anger who glare whenever they see each other and die of rage
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The gods of malicious anger have great hatred together; they glare at each other whenever they meet, and die of rage." Venerable Miào Jìng: you glare at me, I glare back, the anger mounts until one dies.

quiz.q: The first purity of the path lacks "effort of the faculties" due to dull faculties. Plainly put, who is the dull person, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: the lazy — whose wholesome roots are imperfectly cultivated, yet enough to attain the path
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Put plainly, who is the dull-faculty person? The lazy one — whose roots of good are imperfectly cultivated, yet who reaches a level where the noble path can be attained." The *Pixunji*: dull faculties, and no present-life ease.
